contract_plain_english: The source describes finite volume methods as using approximate integrals or averages over grid cells, with a cell average equal to the cell integral divided by its volume. These values change at each time step through cell-edge fluxes, and numerical flux functions are constructed from approximate cell averages to approximate the physical fluxes reasonably well [printed page 5, Section 1.2]. The inherited physical balance states that the time derivative of the conserved amount between two endpoints equals the flux at the first endpoint minus the flux at the second [printed page 4, equation (1.10)]. Integral conservation remains applicable at discontinuities even when the differential equation does not hold classically [printed page 5, Section 1.1.2]. The selected numerical description provides no specific update formula, stencil, or quantitative approximation bound [printed page 5, Section 1.2].
